images.title: Average heights of 19 year olds
images.purpose: Show the chart of average heights of 19 year old boys and girls in 28 countries in 1989 and 2019, on an axis that starts at 145 cm.
images.composition: A wide scatter of markers in country columns, heights up the side starting at 145, countries along the bottom in increasing order, legend at the top.
exact_structure: A vertical axis starting at 145 cm (not 0) with numbered gridlines at 145, 155, 165, 175 and 185, captioned Height (in cm).

28 country columns along the bottom, names written at an angle, in this order from left to right: Timor Leste, Yemen, Bangladesh, Liberia, Indonesia, India, Bhutan, Pakistan, Maldives, Kenya, Saudi Arabia, Japan, Sudan, Taiwan, Italy, Egypt, South Korea, China, Israel, Turkey, Libya, New Zealand, U.K., Australia, Norway, Ukraine, Iceland, Netherlands.
Each column has four markers: vermilion (#D55E00) cross for boys 1989, teal (#0072B2) cross for boys 2019, vermilion triangle for girls 1989, teal triangle for girls 2019.
A legend at the top: B 1989 (vermilion cross), B 2019 (teal cross), G 1989 (vermilion triangle), G 2019 (teal triangle).
rejection: markers for countries in a different order
boys and girls drawn with the same marker shape
images.takeaway: Because the axis starts at 145 cm, distances from the bottom exaggerate differences; read heights from the scale, not from lengths.
images.description: A chart of average heights of 19 year old boys and girls in 28 countries in 1989 and 2019, with the axis starting at 145 cm.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Have students point to the 145 at the bottom before comparing any two markers.

image_decisions.why: The question is about how this chart is organised, including its axis starting at 145.
